reason: The cited lines show the tool obtains a build API via a connection provider and fetches/list artifacts and artifact ZIP contents, returning them as JSON/base64 resources; this supports SECRET because pipeline artifacts are SaaS/build data reached through the configured connection. The returned artifact metadata/content is also user/build-produced content and therefore attacker-controllable in relevant cases, supporting UNTRUSTED. The lines do not show arbitrary host code execution, only API calls and stream/file handling, so HOSTEXEC is not supported. They also do not show sending agent-supplied data to an attacker-readable destination; calls are to the build API and optional local file writing, so SINK is not supported.
